av_event.what: Her voice catches slightly on 'I miss that'. She drops her eyes to the table for a second or two, then looks back up at the camera with a small half-smile.

text:
B: Hello! Oh, hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, I can hear you fine, love. Hiya. I'm Nicola. How are you doing?
B: I'm good, thanks. I'm Claire. Erm, a bit thrown by that puzzle at the start, if I'm honest. How about you?
A: Oh God, the puzzle. I sort of stared at it for ages and then just guessed. Anyway, I'm alright, thanks. Bit stiff today, the weather's been doing my joints in, but I'm fine. Where are you, then?
B: Catford, South East London. And you?
A: St Helens. Between Liverpool and Wigan, if you've not heard of it. I've got to say, I was looking at your photo earlier and I was dying to have a proper nosy at your bookshelf.
B: My bookshelf! Oh, it's a mess, honestly. It's mostly Scandi crime and whatever my book group's made me read. We're doing, erm, a Jon Fosse at the moment, which is sort of hard going.
A: Oh, I tried one of his. Library e-book. It's all one long sentence, isn't it? I had to keep stopping. I'm more of a historical fiction person, and poetry. Carol Ann Duffy, Simon Armitage.
B: Oh, I love Armitage. Do you get through a lot?
A: Loads. It's sort of all I can do some days, to be honest. I'm off work long-term with rheumatoid arthritis, so... I'm not being miserable about it, it's just how it is. The library app's my best friend. Except there's a waiting list on the one I want now, I'm about fortieth.
B: Fortieth! That's brutal. What did you do before, if you don't mind me asking?
A: No, not at all. I was a care assistant in a residential home for years, then a school kitchen. I loved the care work, you know. Sitting with people, hearing the same story about their wedding for the fifth time. I miss that, do you know what I mean?
B: Yeah, I do, actually. That's kind of the bit of my job I like best.
A: What do you do?
B: I'm a housing officer, for a housing association. I've got a patch of about three hundred flats across Lewisham and Greenwich, so it's sign-ups, home visits, rent arrears, neighbour disputes. A lot of it's paperwork, but the visits are where you actually find out what's going on with people. Some days it's lovely, and some days it's, erm, damp and mould and a family of five in a one-bed, and you come home and you can't switch off.
A: Oh, that's funny, I rent off a housing association. Two-bed, me and the two kids.
B: Oh, really? Are they any good? You can be honest, I won't take it personally.
A: They're alright, actually. They took six weeks to fix the back door once, but they put the grab rails in quick when I asked. I think it depends who you get, doesn't it? If you get someone who rings you back, that's half of it.
B: That's exactly it. I'm a bit obsessive about ringing people back. If I say Thursday, I ring Thursday.
A: See, you'd be one of the good ones.
B: I try. What else fills your days, besides the reading?
A: Birds, mainly. I've got a nest box out the back and the blue tits are back in it, I'm made up. And I do little watercolours when my hands let me. I start loads and finish about one in five.
B: That's better than my pottery. I make mugs that come out a weird colour and give them to people who are too polite to say anything.
A: I'd have one! Are those the ones on your top shelf?
B: Yeah, those are the survivors. The green one was meant to be blue.
A: Ah, it's character, that. My Ellie's the creative one in our house now, she's fifteen. She's been doing TikTok recipes, made us a Thai green curry for tea last week and it was actually lovely.
B: Oh, good on her. I keep trying to do Ottolenghi for dinner and it takes me about three hours.
A: Ellie'd have a go at that. Anyway, I'm waffling, sorry.
B: No, not at all, this is nice. I think we've probably not got long left, have we?
A: No, it goes quick, doesn't it? It's been lovely talking to you, Claire.
B: You too. Good luck with the waiting list.
